prompt:
Does any thread of crunch stay runnable but get almost no CPU time for a long stretch (seconds)? If so, which thread, and what keeps it off the CPU?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: yes

## Runnable starvation

Across the whole trace (0–30,517 ms), **calc-3 (TID 636275)** spent **7,515 ms (25.1% of its alive time) runnable but waiting for CPU**, while running for only **2,340 ms (7.7%)**. Ten waits to run lasted at least 10 ms; the longest was **950 ms**.

The main CPU occupant during those waits was **monitor (TID 636280)**, another thread in **crunch**: it held CPUs 6 and 7 for **99.8%** of calc-3’s waiting time and had **real-time priority 10**, while calc-3 had normal priority. This recurring CPU contention made calc-3 the bottleneck: across 18 rounds, it waited an average of **416.7 ms per round** for CPU and finished an average of **416.3 ms after its peers**.
